title: Conversational persona heuristics — personal PRD notes
content:
Quick brain-dump / rough PRD for persona-driven conversational heuristics. Notes to self — very much a work in progress.

Purpose:
- Give product teams a lightweight, opt-in way to define conversational ‘personas’ that bias style, verbosity, and safety heuristics per user segment or route.
- Not a heavy ML feature; mostly runtime prompt + response-shaping policies + small profile store.

Problem we see:
- Different customers want different tones, formality, and factuality tradeoffs (support bots vs. sales assistants).
- Current approach: monolithic prompt engineering and per-customer templates in app code -> duplication, hard to audit, inconsistent rollouts.

Assumptions / hypotheses:
- A central persona layer can reduce duplicated prompt templates by >50% for internal product lines.
- Persona defaults + lightweight overrides reduce time-to-ship for new conversational routes by 30%.
- Safety and compliance policies applied at persona layer will catch 70–80% of simple policy violations before model call.

Target users and personas (examples):
- "Support Minimal": short, procedural answers, include troubleshooting steps, conservative about speculation.
- "Sales Conversational": warmer tone, higher verbosity, uses persuasive language, includes product benefits.
- "Compliance-Strict": avoids user data echoing, redacts PII, refuses certain categories.
- "Research Assistant": verbose, cites sources, longer context windows.

Core feature sketch:
- Persona definition object (JSON-ish): name, tone, verbosity, refusal_rules, allowed_tools, preferred_model_variants, post_processing_rules.
- Simple UI: list + preview (input -> persona preview + sample reply).
- API: attach persona_id to generation request; runtime applies persona-specific prompt wrapper and post-processing.
- Fallbacks: persona -> route default -> org default.

User stories:
- As a product engineer, I can create a persona and preview sample responses so I can standardize tone across routes.
- As an admin, I can pin a persona to a rollout (canary, A/B) to test changes without touching app code.
- As an SRE, I want the persona layer to be a no-op performance-wise (max 1–2ms overhead) and not increase model token usage by more than 5% for typical prompts.

Acceptance criteria (initial):
- Persona schema defined and stored in config store (CRUD APIs).
- Basic runtime that wraps prompts with persona prefix and applies a post-filter for refusals.
- Simple console surface to create/preview personas.
- Metrics: usage counts, token delta per persona, safety-filter hits.

Technical notes / implementation ideas:
- Implement persona prefixing as lightweight template injection. Keep it short to avoid token bloat.
- Post-processing rules implemented as an ordered small rule engine (regex-based + allowlist/denylist), with option to call a small safety model only for borderline cases.
- Cache persona definitions in edge layer (redis or memory) keyed by persona_id for <1ms lookup.
- Attach persona metadata to traces so we can break down latency/cost by persona.
- Consider storing persona-compatible model variants to route lower-cost quantized variants for non-sensitive personas.

Open questions / risks:
- Ownership: should personas live in product teams or platform? (Prefer platform-managed but editable per-tenant.)
- How to version personas safely? Need rollout semantics for persona changes (canary, staged, rollback).
- Security: persona rules must never be bypassable. How to audit and prove enforcement?
- Token cost: longer persona descriptions increase per-call cost. Might need short codes + server-side template expansion to avoid sending full persona every time.

Experiments to validate:
- Pilot with 2 internal routes: support-bot and onboarding helper. Measure time-to-ship and variability in replies.
- A/B test: route responses with persona vs. manual prompt plumbing for same route; metric: consistency score (human evaluation), dev time to onboard.

Telemetry / metrics to capture:
- persona_id usage count by route and org
- avg token delta (persona vs no-persona)
- safety-filter hit rate by persona
- latency overhead distribution
- regression signal: quality deltas after persona change (linked to evals)

Quick sketch of persona schema (notes):
- id: string
- name: string
- description: string (short)
- tone: enum [formal, neutral, casual, salesy, curt]
- verbosity: enum [short, medium, long] or percent target
- refusal_rules: list of rule ids
- post_hooks: list (redact, cite, summarize)
- model_preferences: list (gpt-like, open-llama, quantized-small)
